raw_comment: I noticed that almost everywhere in the US is experiencing some sort of water shortage. It is the most extreme in western Texas and the border between Ohio and West Virginia. Lots of parts of the US are “abnormally dry”, but there are many places that are in the “moderate” or above group. I wonder how this graph looks after widespread rainstorms or hurricanes. I wonder if this graph is always this colored with drought or is it more extreme right now than normal? I wonder if the places that aren’t colored have a normal amount of water or if it just hasn’t been reported. This relates to my community because it has been very dry where I live lately and this graph shows that my state is in the “severe” group which is very abnormal for it. This can help my community prepare and use water sparingly, since we are not used to this kind of drought. It also provides perspective that we aren’t even in the worst of it, but how bad it feels, so it must feel even worse it the “exceptional drought” areas. I would title this graph: Where Did the Water Go?: America is Plagued With Drought
